questions.q: What does a semantic model's item page show, per this lesson?
options: Only the DAX formulas used in its measures, with no owner or label information
A list of every report ever built from the model, with no other metadata
An owner, an inherited sensitivity label, and tabs for Overview, Lineage, Monitor, and Permissions — the same governance surface any Fabric item carries
Nothing — semantic models have no item page of their own
questions.explain: A semantic model is a Fabric item in its own right, carrying the same owner/label/tabs governance surface as any other item.

questions.q: What does Build permission actually let someone do, per this lesson?
options: Only view content that someone else already built from the model
Create new reports directly against the semantic model, in Desktop or the service
Change the workspace's own role assignments for every other item
Delete the semantic model entirely
questions.explain: Build is the permission to create new content against the model, distinct from Read (viewing existing content) and Reshare (granting access to others).

questions.q: Why is Build/Reshare access on a specific semantic model described as separate from a workspace role?
options: Because Build access is granted automatically to every workspace Viewer
Because only Fabric admins, never model owners, can grant Build access
Because workspace roles and model permissions are actually identical settings stored in the same place
Because the model's owner grants it directly to specific people or groups, independent of anyone's workspace role
questions.explain: A workspace Viewer can already read a model in that workspace, but Build and Reshare on that specific model is the owner's own, separate decision.

questions.q: What are the two configurable paths a requester can see when they hit Request access on a semantic model?
options: An email request routed straight to the owner, or written instructions pointing to the real access process
A phone call script read aloud by the Fabric portal
Automatic approval with no owner involvement at all
A single fixed form with no owner customization possible
questions.explain: The owner pre-configures the request dialog as either a direct email or custom written instructions, such as which security group to join.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does a governed request path matter more than an ad-hoc email to the owner?
options: The request — and who approved it — becomes traceable, the same auditability principle applied elsewhere in Fabric
It guarantees every request is automatically granted
It removes the need for any owner to ever review a request
It has no real advantage; it is purely cosmetic
questions.explain: A configured, documented request path keeps access decisions traceable, consistent with the activity-log auditability covered earlier in the course.
